newsitem.title: TAIWAN: POLL-Taiwan June export orders seen up 5.02 pct.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Taiwan June export orders seen up 5.02 pct.

text.p: A Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists on Friday projected 5.02 percent year-on-year growth in June for Taiwan's export, with the strong electronics and information sectors setting the relatively modest pace.
The figures were to be released by the economics ministry at 0230 GMT on July 22.
In May, export orders rose 4.21 percent year-on-year.

Economists said they expected stable growth in June export orders as Taiwan's information and telecommunication industry has continued to attract buyers.

"June's performance would not be too good as June traditionally is a weak-sale season, though the information and telecommunication industry should still perform well," said Core Pacific Securities economist Lin Yang-chuan.
The Taiwan dollar's slow but steady recent depreciation against the U.S. dollar and Japanese yen should help boost local exporters' competitiveness worldwide, economists said.
They said they expected export orders to enjoy higher growth starting July as high-technology industries would enter a hot-sale season.

"Taiwan's export orders should have higher growth starting July as Intel is slated to cut microchip prices soon, a move that would trigger big increases in orders for Taiwan's electronics and information industry," said International Investment Trust economist Hung Chao-lung.

Economists said order growth would be offset in part by a US$130 million a month reduction in foreign orders for pork, as Taiwan continues to tackle an islandwide outbreak of a hog foot-and-mouth disease detected in late March.
